Shigatse|China.f: Shigatse is home to Tashilhunpo Monastery, traditionally the seat of the Panchen Lama.

Ezhou|China.f: Under Sun Quan, Ezhou became the capital of the state of Eastern Wu and was renamed Wuchang.

Qiqihar|China.f: Qiqihar takes its name from a Dagur word meaning border or natural pasture.

Ordos|China.f: Legend says Genghis Khan dropped his whip while passing through the Ordos area on his way to conquer Western Xia.

Yuncheng|China.f: Yuncheng's Hedong Salt Pond is called the earliest salt pond developed in the world, mined for over 4,600 years.

Zhanjiang|China.f: In 1898 France forced China to lease the Zhanjiang area for 99 years as Guangzhouwan, known as Fort Bayard.

Datong|China.f: Datong's locomotive works built about 4,689 of the 4,717 QJ steam locomotives, still being made as late as 1988.

Jiayuguan|China.f: The fortress at Jiayuguan stands at the end of the Ming Dynasty section of the Great Wall of China.

Yiwu|China.f: More than 60% of the Christmas trinkets sold worldwide in 2013 reportedly came from Yiwu.

Baotou|China.f: The warrior Lu Bu, a famous figure of the late Han dynasty, was born in what is now Baotou's Jiuyuan District.

Dunhuang|China.f: The Mogao Caves near Dunhuang have also yielded Christian, Jewish and Manichaean artifacts from the Silk Road era.

Lianyungang|China.f: Donghai County, part of Lianyungang, holds 70% of China's natural crystal reserves and makes 80% of its crystal products.

Huai'an|China.f: Huai'an was linked to Suzhou by the Han Canal, completed in 486 BC by Fuchai of Wu to ease his supply lines.

Yancheng|China.f: Yancheng means Salt City, and sea salt was gathered on the fields around it as early as 119 BC.

Hailar|China.f: Near Hailar lies a huge underground Japanese fortress, completed in 1937 by forced Chinese laborers.

Zhangjiajie|China.f: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, part of the Wulingyuan Scenic Area, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992.

Huangshan|China.f: More than 20,000 poems were written about Mount Huangshan between the Tang and Qing dynasties, and a school of painting bears its name.

Luoyang|China.f: In 166 AD the first Roman mission, sent by Marcus Aurelius, reached Luoyang after arriving in China by sea.

Zhoushan|China.f: The Zhoushan Archipelago has 1,390 islands and 3,306 reefs, making it the largest archipelago in China.

Jinghong|China.f: Mangrai, who founded Chiang Mai in 1296, had a maternal grandfather who was King of Jinghong.

Golmud|China.f: Golmud began in 1954 as a food distribution base staffed by 10 people and is now Qinghai's second-largest city.

Tingri|China.f: Tingri County recorded the lowest temperature ever measured in Tibet, minus 46.4 C on January 7, 1966.

Shiquanhe|China.f: Shiquanhe grew from just over 1,500 people to over 20,000 in the 30 years between 1978 and 2008.

Qamdo|China.f: Some 40,000 People's Liberation Army soldiers attacked the 8,000 Tibetan Army defenders of Chamdo on 7 October 1950.

Daocheng|China.f: Daocheng Yading Airport, in Daocheng County, is described as the world's highest airport.

Kangding|China.f: A magnitude 7.75 earthquake on July 1, 1786 ruined nearly the entire city of Kangding.

Tashkurgan|China.f: In 2013 Chinese researchers announced they had excavated a cluster of Zoroastrian tombs in Tashkurgan.

Maqin|China.f: Maqin County is named after Anye Maqen, the Tibetan name for a revered local mountain.

Yushu|China.f: The official source of the Yellow River lies in Yushu prefecture, which also holds headwaters of the Yangtze and Mekong.

Langzhong|China.f: Under the Han and Tang dynasties, Langzhong was an important center for astronomical research.

Mangnai|China.f: Mangnai is one of China's most remote cities, with the nearest other city, Ruoqiang County, 350 km away.

Xichang|China.f: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake in 1850 killed more than 20,600 people in Xichang.

Shangri-La|China.f: This county was renamed Shangri-La in 2001, after the fictional land in James Hilton's 1933 novel Lost Horizon, to promote tourism.

Xuzhou|China.f: Records show 59 levee breaches near Xuzhou between 1550 and 1855 as the Yellow River flooded the area.

Jiaxing|China.f: The Chinese Communist Party's first congress was concluded on a boat on Jiaxing's South Lake in 1921.

Ninglang|China.f: Ninglang is home to the Mosuo people, often called China's last matrilineal society, who practice walking marriage.

Changzhou|China.f: Changzhou's rebuilt Tianning Pagoda stands 153.79 m tall, making it the tallest pagoda in China and perhaps the world.

Nantong|China.f: Nantong's land was formed over centuries by silt building up at the mouth of the Yangtze River.

Ulanqab|China.f: Since 2016, nearly 100 data centers have opened or begun construction in cold, windy Ulanqab, northwest of Beijing.

Beihai|China.f: After the 1876 Treaty of Yantai, eight Western nations set up consulates, hospitals and customs offices in Beihai.
